## 2. Owning MachineSet and Failover Capacity

The Machine belongs to MachineSet **`larch-6qz4t-gpu-us-east-2b`**.

This is a **single-replica GPU MachineSet** (1 desired / 1 ready / 1 available). There are **no other Machines in this MachineSet** that could absorb workloads during the replacement — it is a sole-instance GPU node.

**Planning implication:** When you drain this node, GPU workloads will have nowhere to land until a replacement Machine is provisioned and joins the cluster. You should either:
- Scale the MachineSet to 2 before the drain (so a second GPU node is ready), or
- Confirm that GPU workloads can tolerate downtime during the replacement window.

---

## 3. Machines in the Same Availability Zone (`us-east-2b`)

The following **5 Machines** are in `us-east-2b` — AWS hardware retirements can sometimes affect the entire zone:

| Machine | Role | Node |

| `larch-6qz4t-gpu-us-east-2b-h7qvd` | GPU worker | `ip-10-0-148-37` ← **this instance** |
| `larch-6qz4t-master-1` | Control plane | `ip-10-0-140-77` |
| `larch-6qz4t-worker-us-east-2b-d8nfl` | Worker | `ip-10-0-152-9` |
| `larch-6qz4t-worker-us-east-2b-k3tqs` | Worker | `ip-10-0-133-188` |
| `larch-6qz4t-worker-us-east-2b-w6vye` | Worker | `ip-10-0-159-41` |

That is 1 control plane node and 3 standard workers in addition to the retiring GPU node. If AWS is retiring a physical rack or host aggregate in `us-east-2b`, all four other machines above could also be at risk. It's worth checking with AWS whether the notice is isolated to the single instance or covers additional hardware in that zone.
